qsSteps:
1. WireGuard tab: paste the complete .conf and enable Auto-Connect.
2. Connection tab: optional TR-064 credentials of the remote FritzBox.
3. Port tunnels: map a local port to the remote device IP.
4. Save and restart the adapter.
5. Use Test connection or open the Web-UI.

For Kostal adapters use host 127.0.0.1 and the local tunnel port.
subnetWarn: Same subnet locally and remotely? Restrict AllowedIPs to required hosts only, for example 192.168.178.30/32 and 192.168.178.31/32, so the local network stays reachable.
connHelp: Optional TR-064 credentials of the remote FritzBox for device list and WAN data. Not required for Kostal tunnels. With identical subnets TR-064 often reaches the local box.
fritzHost_help: IP of the FritzBox at the remote site, usually 192.168.178.1. Do not enter the inverter IP here.
fritzPort_help: Default TR-064 port of the FritzBox interface.
webPort_help: Port of the adapter web interface for monitoring.
wgHelp: Paste the complete FritzBox WireGuard .conf content. Prefer a desktop browser. Restart the adapter after saving.
wgConfig_help: DNS lines and 0.0.0.0/0 are removed automatically. On identical subnets restrict AllowedIPs to single hosts.
autoConnect_help: Recommended: bring the VPN up when the adapter starts.
autoReconnect_help: Recommended: restore the connection after a drop.
tunnelHelp: Forwards a local port to a device in the remote network. Default: only 127.0.0.1 (for other adapters). Enable “LAN access” to open the same port on the host IP for phones/PCs in your LAN. Kostal: host 127.0.0.1, port = local tunnel port (separate fields).
tunnelRestartHint: After tunnel changes: save and restart the adapter or restart tunnels in the Web-UI.
